questionText: Given an integer array of size $N$, we want to check if the array is sorted (in either ascending or descending order). An algorithm solves this problem by making a single pass through the array and comparing each element of the array only with its adjacent elements. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is
explanation:
To check if an array of size $N$ is sorted (in either ascending or descending order) using a single pass, the algorithm makes at most $N-1$ comparisons.

Upper Bound: The maximum number of comparisons performed is proportional to $N$, so the time complexity is $O(N)$.

Lower Bound: In the worst case (for example, when the array is sorted), the algorithm must examine all adjacent pairs (i.e., perform $N-1$ comparisons) to confirm that the array is sorted. Hence, the worst-case time complexity is also $\Omega(N)$.

Therefore, the worst-case time complexity is $\Theta(N)$, which means it is both $O(N)$ and $\Omega(N)$.
